processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental alloys were melted in an induction furnace (alloy fabrication step preceding solution treatment).
Solution heat-treated for 35 min at 1250 °C in a protective argon atmosphere and then water quenched; material then cut into 3-mm (length), 3-mm (width) and 1-mm (thickness) samples.
Annealing treatments were conducted at 500 °C, 700 °C, 900 °C and 1050 °C; holding time not reported for this condition. The 900 °C state of the Ni-containing alloy is this sample.

structures.overall_structure: Duplex ferrite (α) + austenite (γ) matrix. In the γ matrix, coarse NiAl-type B2 particles (2–7 μm) and grain-boundary B2 (GB-B2) form; in the α ferrite, nano-sized disc-like NiAl-type B2 (≈200 nm) forms. No κ-carbides are present at 900 °C.

phases_present.morphology: coarse particles with flat interfaces and sharp edges; grain-boundary precipitates (GB-B2)
phases_present.grain_size: 2–7 μm (coarse B2 particles); ≈1.4 μm average size

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed nano-sized discs within the α ferrite matrix

interfaces.slip_behavior: According to the Orowan mechanism the increase in shear stress (Δτ) is proportional to the inverse of the precipitates' diameter (Δτ ∝ R^−1.25); the uniformly distributed nano-sized disc-like B2 particles in the α matrix increase the shear resistance of the α-matrix.
interfaces.phase_evolution: At 900 °C and above, in the Ni-containing alloy, B2 forms as micron-sized particles and grain-boundary precipitates in the austenite phase and as nano-sized discs in the ferrite; no κ-carbides form at this temperature (κ only forms at 500–700 °C, where ferrite is replaced by B2 stringer bands).
interfaces.interface_notes: Degree of coherency of ordered phases with their matrix is discussed generally in the paper (b0012) but no specific coherence value is reported for the 900 °C Ni-containing sample.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: nanoindentation arrays of 50–70 indentations across the region of interest
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Nano-indentation at a constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s−1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each measurement in a particular phase repeated at least 25 times.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: At 900 °C the Ni-containing alloy has γ+B2 = 7.9 GPa and α+B2 = 11.7 GPa versus the Ni-free alloy where γ+B2 = 7.2 GPa and α+B2 = 8.9 GPa; the Ni-containing B2-bearing structures are consistently harder.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s−1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN, hold time 20 s; each phase measurement repeated at least 25 times; arrays of 50–70 indentations
characterization_methods.purpose: To determine the nano-hardness of individual phases (solution-treated γ and α, B2 stringer bands, micron-sized and nano-disk B2) and of phase combinations (γ+κ, γ+κ+B2, γ+B2, α+κ, α+nano-disk B2).
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 900 °C Ni-containing sample: γ = 4.1 GPa, α = 2.9 GPa, γ+B2 = 7.9 GPa, α+B2 = 11.7 GPa; precipitate-bearing composites are markedly harder than the parent phases. The technique yields a compound hardness of the matrix with particles, not isolated nano-sized precipitates.

characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM) — selected-area diffraction patterns (SADP) and bright-field (BF) imaging
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2000FX; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in 10% perchloric acid + 90% ethanol at 25 V
characterization_methods.purpose: To characterize the ordered phases (nano-sized disc B2 in α and cuboid κ in γ).
characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM bright-field image of a disk-like B2 particle in the α matrix after annealing at higher temperatures (e.g. 900 °C and 1050 °C).

characterization_methods.technique: field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) with X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss Sigma Field Emission SEM operated at 20 kV, fitted with high-speed X-ray EDS; specimens polished and etched in 5% nital
characterization_methods.purpose: To observe the microstructure (e.g. B2 stringer bands, grain-boundary B2, indentation arrays) and to determine the composition (Ni, Al, Mn contents) of the ordered precipitates.
characterization_methods.key_findings: SEM images show the multi-phase microstructure and nano-indentation arrays (Fig. 3); EDS compositions reported include the Ni content of B2 in the Ni-containing sample.

computational_details.simulation_method: ab-initio DFT (Hohenberg-Kohn formalism), generalized gradient approximation (GGA) of Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) in spin-polarized form
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Ultrasoft pseudopotentials created from a modified Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos (RRKJ) scheme; 18×18×18 Monkhorst-Pack k-grid for structure optimization; 50 Ryd real-space grid cutoff for charge density; augmentation charges expanded to 600 Ryd; 30×30×30 grid with 60 Ryd cutoff for DOS and formation energy.
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Bulk unit-cell (periodic) calculations for ordered phases FeAl-B2, Fe3Al-L12, Fe3AlC-L1'2 (κ), Fe2MnAlC, FeMnAlC, Mn3AlC; dynamic matrices from linear response in the harmonic approximation; DOS by the tetrahedron method with a 30×30×30 mesh.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated lattice parameter of FeAl-B2 (with and without spin effects) was slightly less than the experimental value but in good agreement; the calculated lattice constant of Fe3AlC exceeded that of Fe3Al-L12, consistent with experimental observations; calculated elastic-constant trends (higher Mn content → harder κ) confirmed the experimental hardness values.

analytical_models.equation_role: Fitting simulated unit-cell volumes to obtain the bulk modulus
analytical_models.model_note: Various unit cell volumes were simulated and fitted with a Murnaghan equation of state.

analytical_models.model_name: Elastic constants from acoustic phonon slopes (method 1)
analytical_models.equation_role: Determine C11, C44 and C12 from the [100] and [111] acoustic branch velocities (equations 1–3)
analytical_models.model_note: For cubic systems only C11, C12 and C44 are independent.

analytical_models.equation_role: C11-C12 from a volume-conserving orthorhombic distortion (eqs 4–5); C44 from a monoclinic distortion (eqs 6–7); C13, C33, C66 for tetragonal Fe2MnAlC/FeMnAlC
Compute bulk modulus B0, anisotropy factor Cα, shear modulus G, and Young's modulus E100/E111 from the elastic constants

unmapped_findings: At 900 °C and above, the ferrite (α) phase of the Ni-containing Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni alloy contains nano-sized disc-like B2 particles of Ni-Al type (vs Fe-Al type in Ni-free samples); the discs are of Ni-Al type in the Ni-containing samples.

The nanoindentation technique used cannot measure the hardness of isolated nano-sized precipitates; it measures instead the hardness of the nano-sized features within a surrounding matrix, giving a compound (matrix + particle) hardness value.

According to the Orowan mechanism the increase in shear stress Δτ is proportional to the inverse of the precipitates' diameter (Δτ ∝ R^−1.25); the higher hardness at higher annealing temperatures is attributed to the uniformly distributed nano-sized disc-like B2 particles that increase the shear resistance of the α-matrix.

The higher hardness of the Ni-containing B2 is attributed to the B2 composition being NiAl rather than FeAl, with Ni-Al bonds reported to be stronger than Fe-Al bonds; ab-initio literature values show Ni-Al compounds have larger elastic constants (C11 221.67→375.61 GPa and C44 116.99→133.21 GPa from NiAl to Ni3Al) than Fe-Al compounds.

Increasing the annealing temperature increases the Ni content of the B2 particles: the coarse NiAl-type B2 particles in the γ phase of the Ni-containing sample increase in hardness from 9.1 GPa (Ni: 8.2 wt.%) at 500 °C to 10.5 GPa (Ni: 10.1 wt.%) at 1050 °C.

Calculated elastic constants (Table 3) were related to the experimental hardness: the insertion of a C atom only enhances the elastic constant of the κ-phase (L1'2), while Mn substitution (Fe3AlC → Mn3AlC) increases the elastic constants, confirming the experimental increase in hardness of κ enriched in Mn.
